The precision fence says that anchors computed at the coarser numeric setting must never be printed at the finer tier, and it records that a claim of that sort was caught and corrected. The counting fence says the reading result is a baseline win by counting and nothing more. It sits behind systems trained by gradient methods on one measure, by a chosen design trade, and it points to two published negatives attached to the same reader. The substrate fence says that engineering work on the body does not imply any science gate is met. Continuity across a real kernel swap is owed rather than shown. And coupling the body only to what has been earned is the programme's central open gap, which is parked. The affect fence says the modulator is functional and that feeling is modelled, never felt.

There is no single experiment that passes this page. Its condition is fidelity: every ingredient labelled at exactly its class and no higher, and every recipe inheriting its ingredients' fences. What would sink it is stated as the mirror image: the pantry fails if any ingredient is ever labelled above its class anywhere in the book.

Recorded negatives close the chapter, carried inline by design. The metabolism organ helps foraging and crafting but made building worse in the same live run, and a gate on that stays open. An over-compressed sensory bottleneck lost on data it had not seen, so the fuller set of channels is kept. A simplified factored posterior was built and rejected as lossy, so the exact joint version is used everywhere. The final fence repeats what is not claimed: no demonstration of active inference, no created life, no awareness, no human-level ability — a developmental simulation, a bounded peek, about two of eleven-plus rungs earned.

plain.html:
The last page of the cookbook does two things a recipe book owes its reader at the end. It shows where every figure in the book came from, and it hands the reader a knife.

The provenance half explains that each number, verdict, evidence class and falsifier — the observation that would sink the claim — traces back to a row in a separate ledger of claims, a list added to and never edited. It was merged from many source archives, under rules that only ever move wording down toward what was measured. It records that an honesty audit already calibrated several headline claims downward, and it names them.

The other half is the invitation. For each step the book calls proven, this page states the exact observation that would sink it. Re-run it on fresh data it has not seen, show a baseline was untuned, or pass a task with a trivial shortcut instead. Nothing is exempt.

Between the two halves it prints the honest position again. This is a developmental simulation — a bounded peek at a toy world, never a person — with about two of eleven-plus rungs earned, and the awareness question left open.

clear.html:
This closing chapter is the seal on everything before it. Rather than adding a recipe, it makes the whole book traceable and then invites anyone to knock it down.

It opens by restating the constitution that bound every earlier page. A separate ledger of claims, added to and never edited, is the single source of truth, and where the book and that ledger disagree the book is wrong. Calibration moves wording only downward toward what was measured, including under urgency. A verdict rests on the bound that excludes the threshold rather than on a best estimate. Negative results are content, shown up front, because they are the credibility. No claim is carried above its source evidence class, and a short set of hard limits holds in every chapter: no general intelligence, no awareness, no demonstrated active inference, no created life, no beating other systems.

The four status words are restated, with one point made very firmly. A design does not become a result by being signed off. Every signed design folded into the book enters as designed and not run, raises nothing, and leaves its rung's status unchanged.

Provenance is the heart of the page. Every quantitative figure, verdict, evidence class and falsifier — what would sink the claim — traces to a ledger row. The rows cover the developmental rungs, a separate continuity sub-ladder that is engineering evidence rather than science, a set of method patterns, and a north-star bar. The continuity negatives are carried first-class. A live update on a single box is a seconds-long freeze rather than no downtime, and some external legs do not survive it. An over-compressed sensory bottleneck lost on data it had not seen. A fluency-for-calibration trade is called honest rather than a win, and the bare substrate is missing isolation and decay. The ledger's own maintenance rules are given too: each row takes the weaker class of its parts, corrections are added rather than edited in silence, and the preprint is always cited as mathematics only and marked unrefereed. It records that an honesty audit already calibrated several headline claims downward, naming each one.

Then the honest position, printed without softening: this is a developmental simulation, a bounded peek at a toy world, never a person, with about two of eleven-plus developmental rungs earned. The chapter lists which rungs hold a sealed pass and prints their limits beside them. A first-division result at the coarser numeric tier. A cellular benchmark carried with its named losses. A heart model that is a toy rather than a clinical instrument. An affect model that is modelled and never felt. A reading result that is a counting baseline and not comprehension. A language result always cited beside its own caveat, and a self-model that is functional only. The motor rung carries a sealed positive beside a sealed negative. Several negatives are set out at length, including a wall where comprehension above retrieval has not been beaten across structurally distinct attempts, and a metabolism result that helps foraging and crafting while making building worse. Two rungs are parked, and two are not built at all.

The last section is the knife, and it is specific. Re-run a proven rung on fresh unseen data with several disjoint seeds and watch whether the interval still clears its threshold. Show a baseline was untuned. Collapse a gain by swapping markers. Pass a self-model task with a trivial rule. Show continuity across a real kernel swap and an owed stage is discharged. Every gate names the observation that would sink it, and none is hidden or exempt.

plain.html:
This is the whole cookbook compressed into one document. It is the outline of a single buildable recipe for a complete developmental arc, from conception through metabolism, movement, perception and language and on to open questions about creativity and awareness, all expressed as one engine shown at many scales. It describes a simulation — a bounded peek at a toy world, never a person.

The one thing it says is that the full recipe is recommended and every step is still labelled with what is really there. Each rung gets ingredients, method steps, a pass condition, the result that would sink it, and one honest status word. A separate ledger of claims, added to and never edited, sits beside the plan, and where the two disagree the plan is wrong.

Because it is a plan rather than a report, its most useful section is the one at the end: a list of open questions, ordered by how much each answer would unblock, each now carrying the answer it received. Those answers add designs, not results. Every one is recorded as a gate to build rather than something achieved, and the plan states that adding them raises no rung.

clear.html:
This document is the cookbook in outline. It is the single buildable plan for a developmental arc, running from a first cell division through cellular upkeep, metabolism, an organ model, affect, movement, perception, language and a self-model. From there it goes on to reasoning, wisdom, offline replay and creativity. The unifying claim is modest and structural — one engine, reused at many scales, with only the world and the observation model swapped. The honest position is printed at the top and repeated at the bottom: about two of eleven-plus rungs earned, and the whole thing a developmental simulation.

It opens with the kitchen rules, set out as a table of governance patterns that bind every recipe below and are explicitly not capability claims. Every claim carries an evidence class and a falsifier, the result that would sink it, in a ledger added to and never edited. A bar is registered before the build, and a set kept back is touched once. A claim of reproduction is derived from several seeds rather than written in. Synthetic construction is diagnostic, never capability, and a bound is owed only after several structurally distinct negatives. A capability claim needs a tuned baseline and a check that collapses the gain. A passing test does not satisfy a criterion asking for an observation, and a linter downgrades an overclaim. World, body and mind stay separate, learning is counting with a guard against gradients, and numeric precision is stated honestly. What came from above is not counted as fresh evidence. Negatives are published as the pitch, a panel signs before a merge, and one change is made at a time. A long run is written down as it goes, because silence is not success. A list of standing limits follows, and then the four status words.

A shared pantry table names the engines every recipe draws on, each labelled at its real status. Then the ladder itself is walked rung by rung, and each rung is given the same shape: ingredients, numbered method, an exact gate, an operable falsifier, any recorded negatives inline, and one honest status word. The lower rungs carry passes with their limits and losses printed beside them. The upper rungs are parked or not built, and say so.

A separate section covers the substrate the whole thing runs on, marked as engineering evidence rather than science, with its own negatives carried first-class and its central coupling gap left open. It also records that an honesty audit calibrated several headline claims downward, and instructs the reader to carry the calibrated figures rather than the inflated ones.

The most distinctive section is the last. A set of open questions is listed, ordered by how much each answer would reduce uncertainty about whether a sealed gate could even be defined, and each now carries the answer it received. One refused a phrase and supplied scoped wording instead. One chose which missing primitive to port first. Three proposed first gates for rungs that had none. One proposed the next design on the motor frontier. One installed a framing guardrail for the top of the ladder. Every answer is folded in as designed and not run, and the plan states after each that the rung's status is unchanged.

The provenance note closes it: every figure, verdict, class and falsifier traces to a row in the ledger, no step is labelled above its evidence, no negative is hidden, and any step may be falsified.

plain.html:
This page is the captured record of one consultation on one day. A set of questions prepared beforehand were put to a science adviser, and the answers were written down as given, so that later chapters could point back at them.

The one thing this record says is that the whole session moved wording downward or left it alone, and raised nothing. The stated rule is written into the page's opening: an answer that would lift a claim is recorded but not applied, because a separate record of claims, never edited once written, remains the source of truth.

Most of the answers are designs rather than results. A first gate is proposed for a rung with none. A smallest measurable target is proposed for another that is not built, defined so that it never needs the word people would reach for. A next design is proposed for a motor frontier. A cure is proposed for a gate that is stuck. Every one is signed as a gate to build, and the page says explicitly that adding them raises no status.

The adviser also declined a phrase. It would not sign one form of words that could sound like a mathematical result, and supplied scoped wording instead, along with a list of banned phrasings and their permitted replacements.

clear.html:
This is a dated record rather than a chapter of the cookbook: the verbatim capture of a design consultation, taken so that later pages can cite what was actually said. Its framing rule is stated before the first answer. The answers fold back into the plans calibrated downward only, and an answer that would raise a claim is recorded but not applied. The ledger, an append-only record of claims that nobody edits, stays the single source of truth.

The first answer is a refusal as much as an agreement. Asked to sign a parked frontier as a published exhausted bound, the adviser signed the park but declined that phrase. The reason given was that it could sound like mathematical exhaustion of a design space when what exists is an empirical negative over a tested envelope. Replacement wording is supplied in full, scoping the result to the recorded corpus, splits, metrics, implementation, budget, ablations and baselines, and saying outright that it does not show that no future model could improve. Four banned phrasings are paired with permitted ones. Several conditions are attached that must hold for the park to stay honest: completeness of the record, fairness of the baselines, containment of the metric, and no drift from no tested variant to no possible variant. No rung is inflated, evidence labels stay attached, prose stays subordinate to the ledger, and no claim is made that the theory was demonstrated.

The second answer picks which missing piece of the substrate to port first, and ranks all four with reasons. The chosen one is the learning primitive, vendored exactly rather than reinterpreted, frozen at the version that passed its gate, and proved equivalent by tests. A falsifier is given — a result that would sink the port — including a subtle one: counts could update correctly while the planner still reads the wrong quantity, which would look like learning while failing the actual interface. A list of things that stay unclaimed until the other three land follows, and even after the port the honest status is only that one primitive is literally embodied.

Three further answers are gate designs for rungs that have none. One proposes the smallest target for a rung about reasoning. It tests only whether a slow piece of carried state improves prediction when the local context misleads, with a tuned baseline chosen precisely because it is the one that has so far won. One defines what an offline replay effect would have to measure, with ablations that must collapse the gain and a safety check to catch the case where the benefit was simply extra data. One proposes the next motor design, aimed at a positive rather than at farming another negative, and spells out the conditions under which a clean failure would not even count toward a future bound.

The last answer is the framing guardrail for the top of the ladder. It supplies a paragraph to be published word for word posing awareness as an open question, a list of forbidden phrasings, and a ten-point checklist that any future proposal must clear before it may even be proposed.

The overall sign-off is quoted directly, and it signs the honesty posture with its stated limits preserved rather than signing any capability. The closing exchange records that the park wording and the forbidden phrasings are to be treated as binding red lines for all public copy.

plain.html:
This is a short working document rather than a chapter. It is a prepared package of questions, written to be pasted into a consultation with a science adviser, along with the block of context that has to go first. It records why it exists in this form: the connection needed to run the consultation was not available at the time, so the package was written out and queued instead.

The one thing it says is what the programme most wanted to ask, ordered by how much each answer would unblock. The questions cover how to word a parked frontier so it stays a bound rather than an overclaim. They also ask which missing piece to port first, to close the gap between a coupling rule signed in principle and one that is literally true. They ask what smallest change would move a gate that is stuck. And they ask what smallest measurable target would suit rungs that have no gate at all.

The answer slots are empty. The page also states its own limits plainly: no protected mathematics may be pasted, the framing stays at textbook level, and the output of such a consultation is a private design input rather than something to publish.

clear.html:
This page is a small piece of working apparatus, and reading it as anything more would be a mistake. It is the ready-to-run package for a design consultation: a context block to paste first, then a set of questions ranked by how much each answer would unblock. It records that it was prepared and queued because the browser connection needed to run the consultation was not available at the time.

The context block is worth noticing on its own, because it is the programme describing itself to an outside adviser. It states the honest position: a developmental simulation with about two of eleven-plus rungs earned. It then lists the standing limits it expects to be kept. No claims of general intelligence, awareness, human-level ability or created life. A reading result treated as a counting baseline and nothing more. Synthetic work never inflated into capability. No claim raised above its evidence class. And negatives treated as first-class content. It then summarises which rungs are largely earned, which carry recorded negatives, which are parked, and which are not built and hard-fenced.

The questions themselves map the programme's open problems. How should a parked frontier be worded so that it stays a scoped bound rather than becoming a claim that a search is exhausted or a threshold achieved? Of several primitives missing from the substrate, which single one should be ported first, frozen at the version that passed its gate, to close the gap between a coupling rule signed in principle and one that is literally true? What is the smallest structurally distinct change that would move a metabolism gate which is open and diagnosed as a starvation of information-seeking, and what paired experiment would isolate it one cure at a time? What is the smallest falsifiable target for a rung that has no gate, complete with a tuned baseline, a discriminator that must collapse the gain, and a genuine computed ablation? What smallest downstream gate would make an offline replay effect real without ever needing the word for it? Which structurally distinct design should accrue next on the motor frontier? And what published wording keeps the awareness question falsifiable rather than answered?

The answer slots are left empty, which is what makes this a record of a moment rather than a result. A closing note says what to do afterwards: fold any sign-offs or corrections back into the plans, calibrating wording downward only, record any captured sign-off, and update the progress file.

The page also sets its own limits. Protected mathematics is never to be pasted, the framing stays at textbook level, and the consultation is a private design input whose output is not a publishing surface.

plain.html:
This chapter is about the body a simulation runs on, not about a mind. It describes the physical substrate — real servers on real hardware — that lets a developmental simulation persist. The machine saves its state so a restart resumes it bit for bit. It reads its own telemetry as a kind of sense, learns from an operator's decisions, and acts only after a human approves. The page insists throughout that this is engineering evidence and never evidence about the science, and that it earns no developmental rung.

The one thing it says is where the ladder stops. The mind has not been shown to survive a kernel swap. That step is recorded as owed, and it is written into the middle of the page rather than buried at the end.

It is equally plain about what is missing elsewhere. The rule that the body should embody only what has been earned in the science is signed in principle but not literally true, and that gap is parked behind a design that has not yet been ported. A sensorium is never awareness.

clear.html:
This chapter builds a body, not a mind, and it says so in its own closing words. Its subject is the substrate that lets a developmental simulation keep running on real metal. Its first line and its last are the same: this is engineering evidence, never general evidence about the science, and it earns no developmental rung.

It opens with the same constitution the rest of the book carries. Every claim gets an evidence class and a falsifier naming what would sink it. Claims live in an append-only ledger that nobody edits and that wins any disagreement. Wording is calibrated only downward, negatives are treated as content, and the four status words apply here too. A signed design folded in here enters as designed and not run, and raises nothing.

The recipe itself is a ladder of separate, falsifiable engineering claims, and the chapter is unusual in giving buildable steps. Bring up a small fleet from one image, mesh the machines privately, and give each one its own identity at first boot. Make the mind-state durable. Write it out as bytes and anchor it with a digest, then show that reading it back gives exactly the same bytes and the same next step across a real process boundary, with corruption refusing rather than proceeding. Wire the sensorium so the box reads its own telemetry and files it into a small fixed set of categories rather than into a vector of numbers. Add a mode where the machine can escalate a reasoned request and the operator approves or declines with a reason. A running count of those verdicts shifts what gets proposed next, with the set of safe actions fixed and never self-executed. Gate every change that crosses a machine behind exactly one human approval. Seal a numerical trace and check it comes out identical across different stacks. Ship the isolation pieces.

Each of those has a pass condition and, immediately after, a matching falsifier that names what would sink it. A machine that will not boot. A replay that diverges. A sense channel that stops flowing, or turns out to be the wrong kind of contract. A prior that does not update. A cross-machine change that lands without its approval. A stack that produces a different trace. An isolation piece that is absent.

The negatives are inline and first-class. The central one is that continuity of the mind across a kernel swap has not been shown; what was shown is infrastructure continuity, and a first attempt failed before recovering. A live update on a single box is a seconds-long freeze rather than no downtime, and some external legs do not survive it. An over-compressed sensory bottleneck lost on data it had not seen, so the fuller set of channels is kept. A fluency-for-calibration trade is described as honest rather than a win. The bare substrate lacks tenant isolation and any decay on learned counts.

The largest open item gets its own section. The coupling rule — that the body should embody only primitives earned in the science, frozen at the version that passed — is signed in principle but not literally true today, and the chapter lists exactly what is absent. A signed design proposes porting one learning primitive first, vendored exactly rather than reinterpreted, behind an equivalence gate. It has not been ported, it discharges nothing, and the gap stays parked.

plain.html:
Rocks open the nature sequence, and the first thing they do is set the calibration for everything after. Nobody here did the measuring. Geologists did, and this chapter only cites them, so it is not one of the programme's own results. It also prints an explicit list of what is not claimed, beginning with any suggestion that a rock senses, remembers or infers anything at all.

That refusal is the subject as well as the boundary. A crystal records the conditions it grew in, at extraordinary fidelity, across an enormous span of time — and never reads back what it recorded. Storage is not inference. The reading back happens in the person doing the measuring.

A second trap hides in shared vocabulary. A crystal settling really does minimise a free energy, but not the kind that appears elsewhere in this book. Two quantities wear one name, and sliding from one to the other is a pun rather than an argument.

Every number carries a source you can check or is written down as not measured. Several are recorded as withdrawn or superseded, including one that the chapter's own brief had asserted and instructed be checked.

clear.html:
The nature chapters begin here, with the one that sets the calibration for all the rest. Its subject is the mineral substrate, and its role is to be the reference case for something with a boundary but no model of the world beyond it. The science is borrowed: geologists measured it, this chapter cites them, and it is not one of the programme's own results. Its closing pages carry a long list of what is not claimed.

It begins by showing that even the definition of a mineral frays under inspection. The governing definition is a committee's operational one, hedged on purpose, non-retroactive, and curated — so a species count is the state of a list somebody keeps rather than a fact about the Earth.

Then comes the chapter's spine, which is genuinely elegant. One building block, one rule about how those blocks may join, and the entire silicate kingdom falls out with no free parameters. Count how many corners a unit shares and you generate the classes in order, from isolated points through pairs, rings, chains, sheets and frameworks. The chapter then observes that the temperature order in which these minerals crystallise out of a cooling melt — established separately, by melting experiments rather than by structure — is that same order. Cooling is linking. It marks the limits of the correspondence carefully: the ordering is observed, the causal story is modelled, and the series applies to one starting composition rather than being a law.

A second theme is scope. The number of essentially different ways matter can be periodically ordered in three dimensions is a closed formal result, which the chapter calls a gift, because it means the space of possible structures is finite and written down. It then spends more time on the counterweight: a phase was found with an order forbidden in every one of those groups, because it is not periodic. The word periodic was an axiom nobody restated, so a replicated observation was dismissed for years for contradicting a result whose premise had gone quiet. That episode is recorded as the reference case for forgetting a scope condition.

Other sections show the same discipline applied to particular numbers. A hardness scale that is ordinal cannot be averaged or differenced, and the chapter supplies a clean rank inversion to show it. Unusually, it also names a second inversion it refuses to use, because the sample was the wrong kind, so nobody re-imports it. Two determinations of the same point are carried side by side with an instruction not to average them. The Earth's interior is presented as something inferred from data under a chosen parameterisation, with one value flagged as an input the model was handed rather than a result it earned.

The boundary analysis is the chapter's core. A rock has a boundary and internal states, but nothing inside it stands in for anything outside it for its own use; it has no actions, no preferences, and no temporal depth. It is a write-once medium with no reader.

The recorded negatives are unusually candid. A widely repeated claim about how many minerals require life was withdrawn by its own authors, and is recorded as wrong rather than repeated. The corrected version puts water ahead of life, and even that correction rests on one unreplicated survey, with both figures given as lower bounds. Unfalsifiable claims about crystals are recorded without mockery, alongside the real and stranger things nearby. And it closes by saying again that citing geology is not evidence for anything the programme claims.

plain.html:
Water gets a spec sheet here, as the medium every other nature chapter quietly assumes. All of it was measured by chemists elsewhere, so it contributes no evidence to the programme's own results. It closes with a list of what is not claimed, starting with any suggestion that water is fine-tuned, purposive, or evidence of anything beyond chemistry.

The argument is that water is no neutral background but a pile of anomalies, and that life is built on them rather than in spite of them. A corollary runs through every section: the right account of what water does is usually about the water, not about the thing dissolved in it. Several familiar popular explanations are marked wrong even where their conclusions are right.

Then the contrast the chapter states outright — water attracts more unearned mysticism than any other substance while being, measurably, stranger than the mysticism. Disputed claims get handled carefully rather than dismissed. One famous result died when the samples were blinded. One controlled study turns out to have measured how appealing chosen photographs looked, rather than any property of water. One much-hyped phenomenon is split three ways: a real effect, a contested explanation, and a health claim with nothing behind it. Collapsing those three into one verdict, in either direction, is itself the defect.

clear.html:
This chapter treats water as a component with a specification rather than as scenery. Nobody here measured any of it: the numbers are published chemistry, cited, and not one of the programme's own results. It also ends with a plain list of what it does not claim, beginning with any hint that water is fine-tuned or made for us. Its structural claim is that water's biologically load-bearing behaviour follows from the shape of its hydrogen-bonded network, and that in each case the right thermodynamic account is about the water rather than about whatever is dissolved in it. It grades itself as modelled: individual rows carry their own classes, but the chapter as a whole composes measured constants through stated assumptions.

The sections work through the consequences one at a time. Liquid water is densest a little above its freezing point rather than at it, which is why ice floats and why a lake does not freeze solid from the bottom. It holds a great deal of heat for its volume, which makes it thermal ballast, and the chapter attaches corrections to that rather than leaving it as a slogan. It costs a great deal to evaporate, which is what makes evaporative cooling work. It has a strong surface skin. It dissolves things — and the chapter is careful to say that the popular explanation of dissolution as water simply pulling harder is not the right account. Its network rearranges astonishingly quickly, on a timescale so short that any claim about water holding a configuration has to reckon with it. And the effect that drives assembly of membranes and folding is given at length as, in the chapter's words, the most botched explanation in popular science.

What would refute it is stated structurally rather than row by row. Exhibit a liquid with the same network that lacks the package of anomalies, or one without the network that has them all. Or overturn the thermodynamic account of the assembly effect at small scales. Individual numbers falling outside their stated scope move only their own row.

The recorded negatives are the most instructive part, and the chapter says the record of how each was found is the lesson rather than the verdict. A celebrated claim about water retaining a memory of what had been diluted out of it was re-run in the same laboratory with the same people. The single change that mattered was blinding: with the sample codes sealed, the effect vanished. The chapter draws the careful conclusion — the effect was located in the observer, and the people who found this out did so by running the experiment rather than by arguing. A second claim, about intention changing water, is handled more subtly, because a controlled study exists and reported a positive result. The chapter shows that what it measured was a subjective aesthetic rating of selected photographs, with no physical property of water measured at all, and with the claimant among the authors. A third is split three ways: an interfacial phenomenon that is real and independently replicated, an explanation of it that is contested, and a health claim that has no measurement behind it at all.

The chapter also corrects a widely repeated superlative about water's heat capacity by naming a liquid that beats it, and supplying the condition the usual compilations omit.

plain.html:
Air, here, is a working fluid with a density, a viscosity, a sound speed and a scattering cross-section — not a background. Every value in it was measured by a geophysicist somewhere else. Nobody here did the measuring, and nothing on the page is one of this project's own results. The closing list says what is not claimed, including any suggestion that the atmosphere is regulated, purposive or an agent.

A single property decides whether a body flies or swims, and it is not the one most people would name. Not density, and not stickiness on its own, but the ratio between them — and because air's value sits far from water's, flying and swimming are different regimes rather than one problem at two scales.

Much of the rest is a catalogue of correct laws producing wrong answers. The scattering law that makes the sky blue would, taken alone, make it violet; the missing terms are the sunlight's own spectrum and the eye's response. A rule for how sound fades with frequency holds in one limit and fails badly in real air. And a composition figure is marked as true of one month and nothing else, with a live public fact sheet quoted carrying a value decades out of date to show it.

clear.html:
This chapter builds a specification for the gas everything else sits in, and its spine is a comparison. None of the science in it was measured here: it is published geophysics, cited, and not one of the project's own results. It closes with a list of what it does not claim, beginning with any suggestion that the atmosphere is regulated or purposive. Air and water are set side by side, and the chapter argues that the number deciding which regime a body lives in is the ratio of stickiness to density rather than either alone. Because that ratio differs greatly between the two fluids, flight and swimming are separate problems rather than the same problem rescaled. What would refute it is stated in exactly those terms. Find two geometrically similar bodies matched on the relevant dimensionless number whose flow, forces and control still differ systematically, and the spine is wrong. Compressibility is named in advance as the escape hatch a refutation must avoid.

Along the way it does the derivations. It works out how thick the atmosphere is from first principles. It treats sound, including how absorption depends on frequency and humidity. The tidy rule people quote fails in real air at everyday frequencies, because relaxation in the molecules takes over. The worked numbers show the measured change falling far short of what the rule demands, and a humidity dependence that rises then falls, which no such rule can produce. It treats light, and gives the sky's colour as its cleanest example of a correct law giving a wrong answer through a dropped term. It treats the atmosphere as a heat engine and gets a dimensionless payoff out of it. It notes that the oxygen content has a history rather than being a constant.

Two contested regions are handled at length and neither is resolved. The idea that high oxygen allowed very large insects is presented with the serious mechanism behind it, and with a recent measurement that attacks it at the delivery endpoint. The chapter is equally firm that the mirror-image overrun is inadmissible: showing one mechanism fails one test is not showing the factor was irrelevant. Print both citations or neither. Similarly, the idea that the planet's atmosphere is regulated is split in two. That the atmosphere sits far from chemical equilibrium is treated as replicated and independent of any theory. The regulation claim is marked hypothesised, with a live and unanswered objection about what could possibly be doing the selecting. The chapter adds that contempt is a defect exactly as much as credulity is, and that the limit goes on the claim rather than on the claimant.

The boundary analysis places air outside the body, as a slowly changing external state — something a body senses and is pushed by, without air modelling anything in return.

The recorded negatives include a famous folk claim about which way water turns down a drain, refuted by a dimensionless estimate rather than by a sneer. It is then rescued in the only regime where the underlying physics can win, in an experiment whose long settling time was the whole point. A published mass estimate spanning nearly an order of magnitude is marked inadmissible as a point estimate, with an instruction to quote the spread whole rather than rounding it inward. And a model showing a regulating mechanism is possible is marked as a category error when it is offered as evidence that the mechanism is running.

plain.html:
A provenance chain for the matter a cell is made of is what gets built here. It is an audit trail running from a proton to a carbon atom to a gold atom, with a source on every link and an explicit mark wherever the chain is open. Astrophysics is cited here, not measured, so nothing in it moves the programme's own record of what has been shown. The closing list spells out what the chapter does not claim, including the fine-tuning gloss its most famous story attracts.

Its spine is why heavy elements exist at all in time to matter. Heavier stars burn out far faster than light ones, and the steepness of that relationship is what puts their products back into circulation quickly enough for a later planet to be made of them. The chapter states that as its structural claim and gives the model that would refute it.

It is unusually hard on its own best stories. The famous prediction of a nuclear energy level is corrected: the anthropic version of the tale is marked inadmissible as history, and the real version, resting on a measured abundance, is described as stronger. And a widely repeated claim that a particular observation measured where gold comes from is recorded as false, against the chapter's own commissioning brief.

clear.html:
This chapter treats a star as a machine with a specification and traces where the atoms in a cell came from. Every number in it was measured by someone else and is cited here, so it is not one of the programme's own results. Its closing list names what the chapter does not claim, including the fine-tuning gloss its most famous story attracts. Its declared structural claim is causal: because a star's lifetime falls steeply with its mass, massive stars finish quickly, and that speed is what makes heavy elements available on a timescale short compared with the age of the galaxy. What would break it is written out as a specific alternative. Produce a self-consistent model of galactic chemical enrichment in which massive stars live as long as the Sun and the observed composition still comes out right, and the spine is gone.

It starts with the one equation that holds a star up: its own pressure gradient against its own weight, with nothing exotic required. Before that, the condition under which a cloud collapses at all. The chapter openly names the known sleight of hand in the standard derivation rather than hiding it, keeping it as a working criterion while marking it as not rigorous. Then the organising diagram that sorts stars by brightness and colour, and the scaling of brightness with mass. Here the chapter corrects the textbook: the single exponent everyone quotes is not any of the calibrated pieces measured across the mass range, and the sequence does not even move in one direction. It is usable as a rough device and inadmissible as a measurement.

A section is given to the temptation to link this scaling to the way metabolic rate scales with body mass in animals. The chapter refuses it, and explains the refusal: the claim as stated is unfalsifiable, the two relationships bend in opposite directions relative to proportionality, and power laws are the generic output of scale-free constraints anyway. It is recorded as a rhyme, and the refusal is presented as the method.

Then the burning itself. Which reactions run at which temperatures, the prediction of a nuclear energy level that made carbon production possible, why fusion stops around iron, and how the elements beyond iron are made by slow and rapid capture of neutrons. The chapter is careful about what a celebrated merger observation showed. A lighter element was identified, while the heaviest ones were searched for and not found. Their origin in such events remains an inference from an abundance pattern rather than a detection. There is a section on the brightness limit above which a star blows its own material away, and one on the way the Sun rings, which is how its interior is inferred at all.

The negatives are pointed. A famous story about anthropic reasoning is corrected as history. A claim about which nucleus is most tightly bound is shown to be true of one quantity and false of another, with the defect being the failure to say which. Several standard values are printed with a flag saying their primary sources were not read in this pass, and three genuinely open problems are printed as contested rather than adjudicated, because the chapter says it cannot adjudicate them.

The chapter grades itself as modelled: individual rows carry their own classes, but the chapter as an artefact composes measured constants through stated assumptions into one traced chain from star to cell.

plain.html:
The molecule is taken as what it physically is: a polymer with measured dimensions and mechanics, carrying a measurable amount of information at a measured error rate, packed and copied at measured rates. The molecular biology is quoted from other people's work, not produced here. None of this project's own results stand on any of it. The closing list names what is not claimed, first among them that this molecule is a program, code or blueprint.

That refusal is also the warning. Reading the molecule as source code is marked inadmissible, because no observation could refute it. The chapter's own numbers show why it misleads. A designer who believes it looks for a specification where there is only a starting bias, expects fixed behaviour where the chemistry depends on context, and treats most of the substrate as dead weight.

Its best engineering lesson is about layers. The overall accuracy is not bought by building an excellent component; it is bought by stacking several cheap, unimpressive stages whose failures are independent. That is the structural claim, and what would have to be shown to break it is named.

Several of its own earlier errors are corrected in public, including a misattributed quotation and a rung of its own ladder that was arithmetically impossible.

clear.html:
This chapter is about a molecule and refuses to let the molecule become a metaphor. None of the biology here is ours: it was measured elsewhere and cited, so it is not one of the project's own results. A list at the end names what the chapter does not claim, starting with the idea that this molecule is a program or a blueprint. It opens with geometry at the resolution a designer would actually need, then treats it as a polymer with real mechanics, then gets to information content — and immediately deflates it, because that is where the expensive mistakes live.

Its structural claim is an engineering one and it is stated as such: the system-level performance comes from composing cheap layers whose failures are uncorrelated, not from any component being excellent. What would refute it is written concretely. Show a single replication component reaching the system-level accuracy on its own with the later stages disabled. Or show a large genome copied within one measured window from very few starting points, so that the throughput was bought by speed rather than by parallelism. Either would move the chapter. Individual numbers falling outside their scope move only their own rows.

The sections then walk the stack. First the error budget in layers, which the chapter calls its best engineering lesson. Then the packing hierarchy that fits a great length into a tiny volume, and the arithmetic of copying that makes a huge genome tractable at all. Last the code itself, where the redundancy is argued to be structure rather than noise. The central organising story of molecular biology is given with its genuine exceptions rather than as a slogan. A reading of all this through the book's inference framing is offered explicitly as hypothesised and as a lens only.

The recorded negatives are unusually self-implicating, and that is what makes the chapter worth reading. A famous record-holding genome size is marked inadmissible, with the defect located not in the original measurement — which was honest for its era and its method — but in continuing to cite it today. Two different error rates with different denominators are flagged as not comparable, and a widely quoted figure is shown to be the rate after several layers rather than the rate of one component. A ladder of figures is printed with an explicit note that two source measurements were not reconciled in this pass, and that no reconciliation is being offered. The stacking principle survives, but the individual figures do not travel without the assay that produced them.

Then three corrections of the chapter's own previous text. A decomposition into powers of ten was attributed to the wrong source and printed inside quotation marks, and the chapter says plainly that a quotation mark is a claim about a source and that this one was false. One step of the ladder was arithmetically impossible against its own stated gain and had been graded as if measured. And an explanation of two disagreeing values as a midpoint between different conditions was wrong, because both were assays of the same quantity under the same nominal condition, leaving a genuine method-dependent disagreement unreconciled.

A structural feature drawn in every textbook is marked negative as an in-life claim, because two independent near-native methods fail to find it — it is real in the test tube, and the diagrams are ahead of the evidence.

plain.html:
A single motile cell read as a design exercise rather than as biology appreciation: carry one payload to one target, through a medium that is thick, hostile and unmapped, with no chance to repair or rebuild after launch. Other people's laboratories produced every number, so this is not one of the programme's own results; the chapter does not claim a sperm decides, wants, seeks, knows or navigates in any sense involving experience.

The physics writes most of the requirements before any designer gets a say. At this scale a stroke that simply reverses itself gets you nowhere, so a travelling wave is not a stylistic choice but the only option left. That is the structural claim, and precisely what kind of swimmer would refute it is stated.

Conditions are treated relentlessly. A rate quoted without the thickness of the fluid and the temperature is not a number at all, and two very different beat frequencies are shown from the same cells. Several repeated figures belong to another species, prepared differently, under a load that gets dropped when they travel.

The efficiency is honestly terrible, and that is the instructive part. A popular story about a fighting caste was tested and did not reproduce; a racing story is inadmissible because nothing in it could be refuted.

clear.html:
This chapter treats a single motile cell as an engineering problem with an unforgiving specification. The numbers all come from other people's laboratories and are cited, so this is not one of the project's own results. The vehicle is finished at launch — no transcription, no repair, no rebuild — so whatever machinery it shipped with is all it will ever have, even though fuel can be drawn from the medium along the way. The environment is viscous enough that inertia is irrelevant.

That regime is the chapter's spine, and it insists you do the arithmetic before drawing anything. At this scale a shape sequence that simply retraces itself produces no net movement at all, which rules out whole families of design. What would refute it is written out with unusual care. Exhibit one swimmer achieving sustained progress in an ordinary fluid using a strictly reversible stroke, with the fluid's behaviour measured and the obvious loopholes excluded. The chapter names in advance the escape that does not count, because a springy fluid is already inside the theory rather than a refutation of it.

From there it works through the machine. The motor slides rather than bends, and the chapter is precise about that distinction. A section is given entirely to the principle that a rate without its condition is not a number, and the demonstration is two very different beat frequencies measured from the same cells at the same temperature. Efficiency is reported as poor and treated as instructive rather than embarrassing. Where the energy actually comes from turns out to have been genuinely contested, and the chapter carries the contest rather than settling it. An experiment that disabled one pathway produced immobile cells with the other pathway intact. That overturned the obvious anatomical inference in one animal and leaves the human case unsettled, so neither may be asserted.

Navigation is read as inference, with the act of moving to sample a gradient treated as an epistemic action. The chapter puts a limit on that phrase the moment it uses it: it does not claim a sperm decides, wants, seeks or knows anything in any sense involving experience. The description is statistical: a policy weighted partly by what it would resolve, and a helix that is a sampling geometry. The chapter then examines the folk explanation of why such a cell samples over time rather than across its body. It separates three claims with three different statuses. There is the mechanism actually reported, and a modelling argument that reaches the same conclusion for a different reason. The popular version is recorded as unearned in the form it is usually given.

The recorded negatives are careful about their own wording. A hypothesis about a specialised non-fertilising caste made a testable prediction; the test was run and the prediction did not reproduce. The chapter insists on matching the source exactly, noting that the authors hedged to unlikely rather than refuted, and that some signal was seen but none of it in the predicted pattern. It says this bullet exists to celebrate honesty about a negative result, which is why the wording must be exact. A racing narrative is marked inadmissible because nothing in it could be refuted, and the competing accounts are printed and left unresolved. Several borrowed constants are flagged as belonging to a different species, differently prepared, at a stated concentration and load — all four conditions being easy to drop.

plain.html:
Coordination that lives in the shared environment rather than in any component's model of the whole — that is the system taken apart here. Other people did this entomology and the chapter quotes them. Nothing here is one of this project's own results. It also sets out plainly what it does not claim. Because ants are the book's favourite example, it is hardest on them.

The colony carries something across decades that no individual is present for or could represent. Workers outside the nest live days or weeks; the colony lives for years and changes over that span. Three observations are named that would break that claim, including an individual whose state predicts the colony-level variable better than the shared chemical field does.

Then it dismantles the popular version of its showpiece. The famous shortest-path experiment was a choice between two branches, not a route-planning problem. The mechanism was a difference in travel time, not evaporation; evaporation came later, added by engineers. And pointed at the hard problem it is famous for, the resulting method did not beat a tuned specialist baseline; where it holds records, the win rides on a hybrid with a hand-built local search. That is a negative result about bio-inspiration, recorded in the chapter that likes ants most.

clear.html:
This chapter treats a colony as a distributed system and holds it to the same evidential standard as everything else in the book, which for once cuts against the book's own favourite illustration. The entomology is all borrowed and cited, so it is not one of the project's own results. The chapter also says outright that it does not claim a colony is cognitive. Its own grading of the evidence is contested rather than settled, which is unusual here and deliberate.

The thesis is about levels. Workers outside the nest persist on the order of days or weeks; the colony persists for years and shifts its behaviour over that span. So the colony carries a trajectory no worker is present for. The chapter writes out three concrete findings that would refute it. Find an individual whose internal state predicts the colony-level variable better than the shared stimulus field does. Show the long-run change disappears once worker turnover is held constant. Or run a marking study controlling both named biases that finds outside workers persisting on the colony's own timescale.

It then explains coordination without a plan or a planner: individuals modify a shared medium, and the medium coordinates the next individuals. The famous two-branch experiment is reported as it was actually run, with its decay constants given properly and with intervals rather than point estimates. Crucially, the chapter publishes the trap inside its own favourite result: when the short branch is added after the long trail is already laid, the colony mostly cannot switch. The same positive feedback that finds the shortcut locks in the first answer, and any distributed design lifted from that experiment inherits the lock-in. The chapter calls this the most useful sentence in the paper and the one least often repeated.

Three conflation traps follow. Solving a two-way choice is not solving a route-planning problem over a graph, and the engineering method that does address the latter needed memory, quality-weighted deposition and evaporation, none of which the animals or the original model have. The mechanism behind the discovery was a difference in travel time, not evaporation — evaporation was added later, by an engineer, explicitly as a useful form of forgetting. And when the method was scored against a tuned specialist baseline it lost, with its own authors recording that the fix was to make successors less and less biologically inspired. Where it holds world-class results, the win depends on a hybrid. The chapter records that as negative for one problem, positive for another, and never as nature-inspired therefore better.

A scaling headline about colony metabolism gets the same treatment. The quoted exponent is indistinguishable both from the value it is cited to support and from no scaling at all. Its interval is wide, the sample is small, and a later study across many species refutes any single exponent. The chapter names a different row as the one actually carrying the argument.

Task allocation supplies what the chapter calls the cleanest evidence of a level above the individual. The boundary analysis asks what the colony treats as inside itself and what as outside, and it is done honestly — including the admission that the quantity the chapter's own title rests on has not been measured. A live controversy about the origin of this kind of society is carried and not resolved. And two appealing slogans are marked inadmissible as posed, with the refusal aimed at the form of the claim rather than at whoever asks it.

plain.html:
Falsifiable science on something you can never observe, tested on the hardest case available: animals long dead, that nobody has ever seen move or breathe. Palaeontology is cited here, not measured. The closing list says plainly that no mass, speed or body temperature in it is claimed as known, and that anything believed about colour, sound or behaviour without a preserved correlate is not claimed at all. The animals are the worked example; the method is the payload.

A fossil constrains a quantity only through a physical relation that outlived the animal, so every estimate must be published as an envelope whose width is itself the result. A figure with no method and no error bar is not wrong so much as unevaluable: nothing about it could be refuted.

Its showpiece is a way of estimating speed from footprints — and its most valuable moment is that the method was recently tested against living birds walking on mud and came out too fast by a wide margin. That is a published negative; the method is still taught because it was testable enough to fail, and the test is scoped rather than widened.

Most strikingly, it lists the errors an earlier draft of itself committed, each one exactly the defect it names elsewhere in its own voice.

clear.html:
This chapter picks the hardest possible subject on purpose. You cannot run the experiment; the animal, its soft tissue and its behaviour are all gone. What remains is part of a skeleton, some footprints, and physics that has not changed. Everything the chapter does follows from that. None of the science is ours: palaeontologists did the work and the chapter cites them, so it is not one of the project's own results. It does not claim that any mass, speed or body temperature in it is known.

Its structural claim is epistemic rather than zoological. A fossil constrains a falsifiable quantity only through a physical relation that survived the animal. Every resulting estimate must be published as an envelope whose width is part of the result. It says what would break that. One quantity determined to a stated precision by a method that routes through neither a surviving constraint nor a living calibration animal, and that survives an independent test against a living organism.

The sections work outward from a constraint that cannot be negotiated, through what the bones actually do, to mass — where, unusually, the spread is the answer rather than an embarrassment. The showpiece is estimating speed from trackways: the chapter derives it, works an example, and then deliberately breaks it. A recent test against two living birds on mud found the standard equation overestimating by a wide factor. That is recorded as a first-class published negative and carefully scoped, since the test involved one species on one kind of ground and the authors themselves ask for a broader range. The method stays worth teaching precisely because it was testable enough to fail.

Respiration is presented as a hypothesis that predicted where particular holes in the bone would be, which is the kind of risky prediction the book values. Thermal biology is carried as a live disagreement rather than resolved. Necks get the arithmetic and an honest accounting of what they cost. And the chapter closes the loop by noting that one lineage never stopped running.

The recorded negatives are the chapter's most distinctive feature. The headline inadmissibility is any figure quoted with no method and no envelope. The chapter is careful to locate the defect correctly: the commonly quoted mass actually sits inside a published conclusion, so what is missing is not accuracy but a stated method and range. It also confesses that an earlier draft got that wrong in the opposite direction, refusing a figure as unsourced while its own cited primary asserted it, and names that as its own rule run backwards.

Then it lists, item by item, what a previous draft of itself did. A scope error that inflated a spread. A table misread across rows. A central conclusion left out in a way that made the disagreement look wider than it is. An invented error bar where the published interval was far wider, an exponent altered repeatedly, and a class inflated from two animals to a whole group. Two circular checks presented as corroboration, a false claim that something was unmeasured, and a citation attributed to the paper that quoted it rather than the one that produced it. The chapter says the failure mode is the point.

plain.html:
Two instruments get built out of one animal. Marine biology is cited throughout, so the chapter contributes no evidence to the programme's own results. It makes no claim about whales being self-aware or linguistic. Nor does it claim they talk to each other across ocean basins: nobody has measured that, and the chapter says what would settle it. What it does build is a way of asking what sets a maximum once the obvious limit has gone, plus a working model of low-frequency sound as a long-baseline channel for information.

The startling part comes first. The headline number — the mass of the largest of these animals — has never been measured. Not measured badly; never measured. Every figure in circulation is something else wearing that description, and opening with it disciplines everything after.

Its other preoccupation is units. Comparing loudness underwater with loudness in air, without the correction, is not a finding but a missing conversion. Two more traps follow, involving how a level and an angle are conventionally reported. And the chapter records that it committed the third of those itself, in the very section devoted to warning about it. A convention is not a detail, and the trap catches the people who know about the trap.

clear.html:
This chapter uses the largest animal as an instrument twice over. None of it was measured here: marine biologists did the work and the chapter cites them, so it is not one of the project's own results. It makes no claim about whales being self-aware or linguistic. Because floating removes the skeletal-stress limit that constrains land animals, whatever ceiling shows up instead is informative. The chapter's structural claim is that the limit is set by the energetics of gathering a low-level food resource in bulk, rather than by the mechanics of being large. It gives two ways to refute that. Find a large aquatic animal whose foraging efficiency rises with size but which stays well below the ceiling with food demonstrably available. Or measure a mechanical, cardiac, thermal or respiratory limit that binds below the observed maximum. It is careful to note that an existing candidate measurement, from a single animal, is a candidate for the second of those rather than a satisfaction of it.

It opens, though, with a discipline-setting fact: the mass of the largest such animal has never been measured. Everything published is a model output, a reconstruction, or an estimate — and the chapter names which. It then notes the honest kicker that the largest animal eats some of the smallest, and treats deep diving as a problem in gas physiology whose solution was to remove the gas.

The second instrument is sound. Absorption in water rises steeply with frequency, which is why the long-baseline channel is a low-frequency one, and the chapter gives that as a second refutable claim with the measurements that would overturn it.

Then comes the section the chapter cares most about, which is about units. Underwater and airborne loudness are quoted against different references, so comparing them directly is out by a large factor, and a familiar comparison to a jet engine turns out to be a missing correction rather than a finding. Levels quoted as an average are not comparable with levels quoted peak to peak, and the source itself warns about this. A beam angle reported as a half-angle is not the number a reader would compare against, since the convention is full width. The chapter records that an earlier pass of itself printed that angle wrongly, off by a factor of two, while quoting the very source that supplies the warning, in the section devoted to the warning. It notes this is the third instance of the same class and says the pattern is the point.

A further negative is recorded twice over. A teaching source contains an order-of-magnitude error, apparently by mislabelling a value at one frequency as belonging to another. This chapter transcribed it faithfully, gave it the strongest available class with no primary read and nothing marking its limits, and rested its low-frequency argument on it.

A widely repeated claim about calls crossing an ocean is recorded as not measured as stated: a basin-scale range was calculated rather than observed, and the chapter separates emission from communication, and instrumental detection from reception by an animal. It carries this as an open question, says what would settle it, and does so explicitly without contempt.

plain.html:
The keystone chapter of the nature wing explains itself in its first lines. Everywhere else the book lays an abstraction over a system that was not built to expose it; a bat exposes it. A bat spends energy, at a cost you can meter, to get an informative return, and changes what it emits to resolve a specific uncertainty — all in quantities you can put a microphone on. Sensory biologists did the measuring; this is not one of the programme's own results. The chapter is blunt about what is not claimed, including that a bat performs the book's arithmetic, or that this reading is needed to explain anything in the chapter.

Call parameters are read as state-dependent actions rather than fixed traits, each moving in the direction that keeps a particular inference well-posed. That is written as a claim that can fail, with a specific animal described that would break it, and the test ends with an instruction: go and record one.

Its own cheapest refutation is supplied too. An elegant, arithmetically correct explanation for why calls cannot get faster was refuted when someone measured the muscle instead — the right number, for the wrong reason.

Several of the recorded errors are its own, including one where a cited paper said the opposite of what was printed.

clear.html:
This chapter argues that echolocation is where an abstract idea in this book becomes an instrument reading. Sensory biologists did the work and the chapter cites them; it is not one of the project's own results, and it does not claim that a bat performs the book's arithmetic. The idea is that an agent will pay to reduce uncertainty before that reduction pays off in any goal, which is what separates this framework from ordinary control. That term is normally the hardest thing to see in a real animal, because information-seeking hides inside behaviour doing several other things at once. A bat separates them: the emission cost, the parameter change, and the uncertainty being resolved are all separately measurable.

The chapter does the physics first. One calculation relates frequency to wavelength and explains why an echolocator cannot work at the pitch of a voice. What that choice costs is then named rather than glossed. Range becomes time, and from that the overlap problem between an outgoing call and its returning echo is derived rather than asserted.

Then the chapter turns on its own best derivation. The overlap argument gives a tidy limit on how fast calls can be repeated during the final approach, and the number it predicts is about right. It was refuted anyway: measuring the muscle that produces the call showed the actuator binds first. The chapter records this as the exact failure mode the wing exists to catch, a derivation that predicts the right number for the wrong reason.

Its sharpest positive example is the way a bat shifts the frequency it emits so that the returning echo lands in the narrow band its hearing is tuned to — action taken to keep perception well-posed, measured directly. Predicting the sensory consequences of one's own action gets its own section, as does the intensity of the call, which is where the cost of gathering information is actually paid, and where the literature disagrees. The wing itself and the arms race with jamming close the chapter.

The recorded negatives include two that are the chapter's own and are unusually instructive. In an earlier version, a claim that the middle-ear muscles contract before the call begins was the load-bearing premise of a whole section — and the cited paper says the opposite. The chapter traces exactly how the error formed: latencies that the source reported in order to reject an explanation were re-signed into support for a different one, and the resulting sentence read as more precise rather than less. The underlying idea survives on what the paper actually found, which never needed the lead. The second is a figure printed with an uncertainty attached that could not be sourced anywhere, presented alongside another as an unresolved discrepancy. The chapter's verdict is memorable. The plus-or-minus did the damage because it reads as an instrument talking, a hedge is not a citation, and dressing two unsourced values as a live controversy borrows the chapter's own honesty vocabulary to launder them.

Two convention traps follow, on how loudness and how wing shape are conventionally reported, with the same rule as elsewhere: a number without its convention is not a number.

plain.html:
The human body as a set of measured quantities, flattery removed. Every number was measured by somebody else. None of this project's own results stand on any of it. The list at the end is emphatic about what is not claimed — anything whatsoever about consciousness, and any suggestion that humans are the endpoint of anything.

The opening move shows that nearly every famous number about the body — how many cells, how many neurons, how many bacteria live in us — was an unsourced ballpark that survived by repetition until somebody counted. The correction is the lesson, so each is carried with a record of how it was made. In several cases the people who fixed a number could not find any original measurement behind it at all.

The same discipline then goes to the idea that humans are special, and most versions do not survive. On the relationship between neuron count and brain size, we sit where a primate of our size would be expected to sit. The share of energy the brain uses is real, but the conclusion usually drawn from it does not follow, because the cost per neuron is conserved and the share falls out of the arithmetic.

Where something genuinely is exceptional, the chapter says so — and says plainly which questions remain open.

clear.html:
This chapter treats the human body as a specification and refuses to flatter it. The biology is borrowed: other people measured it, and it is not one of the project's own results. Its structural claim has two halves: the famous headline numbers were unsourced ballparks that moved once measured, and human specialness survives none of the scaling checks applied here. What would refute it is written to match. Produce a primary source predating the corrections that actually measured any of those numbers with a stated method and denominator. Or produce a regression of neuron count against brain size that places humans off the primate line.

It opens by showing the same failure happening three separate times. Then it examines a count whose denominator nobody had stated. That turns out to be the whole defect: with a different denominator the famous ratio changes substantially, and the arithmetic was never the problem. It works through the energy budget, including the familiar figure for a person at rest, and then strips the folklore off the brain.

The rebuke section is the chapter's spine. We carry the neuron count expected of a generic primate brain of our size; we are not first in relative brain size; and the distinctive scaling rule belongs to primates rather than to us. The chapter records that as a published negative, and treats it as credit rather than embarrassment. It then dismantles an inference many readers will have made. The brain's share of the energy budget is real. But because the cost per neuron is conserved across primates, that share follows arithmetically from how many neurons there are, and licenses nothing about cognition.

Other sections do the arithmetic where arithmetic is possible: the point at which walking becomes running is computable. Thermoregulation is named as the actual superpower, with the mechanism given rather than asserted. Sensing is given with real ranges. One arrangement of the eye is discussed as a frozen accident, and the chapter separates two claims: a replicated finding rebuts the idea that the arrangement is a disaster, which is not the same as calling it optimal. A patch recovering a loss is evidence the loss was real. A question about birth and pelvis width is presented with three positions in print and the instruction that printing any of them as settled is the defect.

The chapter is also careful about what does not refute it. On one loose cross-species invariant humans genuinely are an outlier. The chapter says so, and applies its own spine to that comparator: the invariant's own species coordinates are averaged values pulled from a mid-century handbook and an encyclopaedia. An outlier on a loose invariant is data about the invariant, not a warrant for specialness.

The boundary section is where the book's cardinal rule lands hardest, and several figures are flagged as not sourced in this pass and therefore not asserted.

The chapter grades itself as modelled. Rows carry their individual classes, but the chapter as an artefact composes measured constants through stated assumptions — a reference body, a chosen lifespan, full evaporation at the skin. It says outright that those assumptions are the limit. It then turns that on itself: an earlier pass printed an unsourced figure that moved a supposed outlier back inside the band, and sourcing the input deleted the reversal. Every number here is treated as a hypothesis generator rather than a warrant, and the closing list of what is not claimed begins with consciousness, which is named and left where it stands.

plain.html:
This one is a question, not a recipe. The header every other chapter carries is deliberately dropped, because this one builds nothing and must never be read as though it did. Nothing here is one of this project's own results. It repeats the project's position unsoftened: what exists is a simulation that learns, in a toy world. Not a person. No claim is made about whether any successor to the human is possible, impossible, near or far. The one job it does is to map the constraints a candidate would have to satisfy, and to state what would refute each claim people make about the subject.

The question, as usually asked, is ill-posed — and that is treated as good science rather than evasion. The phrase presumes a single ladder with humans on a rung. Evolution has no such ladder; it has a landscape defined relative to an environment, and the landscape moves. If you cannot name the environment, you cannot name the fitness, and the word beyond has nothing to refer to. Such a claim is not weak; it has no truth conditions.

What is real is a constraint space, and that part is measurable. Heat, the geometry of wiring against delay, and development are the limits that actually bind — not a shortage of ambition.

clear.html:
This chapter is a register entry for a permanent open question, and its whole design is about not becoming a plan. It carries no building brief, no roadmap, and no target, and states that there must never be one. The science is cited from other people's work, so it is not one of the project's own results. It repeats the programme's own position, and does not soften it: a simulation, a toy world, never a person. And it makes no claim about whether any successor to the human is possible.

Its most useful section is the correction it opens with. Asking what lies beyond a species presumes a scalar ladder, and evolution provides none, because fitness is defined relative to an environment that itself keeps moving. An organism that lost an organ is not less evolved than its ancestor; it is differently adapted, and has had exactly as long to get there. The chapter then gives the sharpest available statistical correction. Complexity has a floor below which nothing viable can go, so a random walk starting against that floor will extend its upper tail over time without being directional at all. The commonest state of life on this planet has not moved. Reading progress off the growth of the tail is reading a boundary condition as a driving force.

The rest is constraints, each sourced and each with a stated way of being shown wrong. Heat is one, and the chapter is careful to say it is heat rather than the theoretical floor on the cost of erasing information, because that floor is so distant it constrains nothing. Signal speed against size is another, and the chapter presents its wiring model as the weakest thing it carries, explaining that the model predicts modularity rather than impossibility, and naming what would refute it. Information, development and metabolism follow. The metabolic section carries an honest disconfirmation of a famous and elegant hypothesis, which did not survive a broad comparative test. The chapter records it as first-class precisely because it is a hypothesis the wing would have liked to be true.

There are sections on which gradients are actually real, on what would have to be true for any claim here to hold, and on how open questions are carried whole rather than resolved.

The central claim is that no environment-independent scalar exists along which the question could even be posed. What would refute it is written as three conditions any candidate quantity would have to meet. It must be computable from an organism alone. It must order known organisms in a way that survives the counterexamples in the chapter's own table. And not merely a redescription of similarity to humans. The chapter says the third condition is the load-bearing one, that every candidate so far fails it, and that this is its actual finding.

Its negatives are pointed. Total neuron count is shown to have failed twice as a proxy, with two studies in the same journal reaching opposite conclusions. A claim about uploading is marked inadmissible in form rather than rebutted, with the chapter noting that serious people hold the position and that the refusal asks for a way to test it rather than dismissing it. A widely quoted figure for how much a person takes in at once drifts across retellings of a single estimate, and is admissible only as an attributed estimate. And a comparison expressed in orders of magnitude is shown to depend entirely on an accounting choice that is usually left undeclared, which the chapter calls a choice wearing a measurement's clothes.

plain.html:
